Sports.title: After dramatic Shaw U-turn and title win, Manchester City target historic Double
Sports.content:
Secure your first league title for a decade? Tick. Extend your golden boot-winning striker’s contract. Tick. Lift a first Women’s FA Cup since 2020? Pending. May 2026 has gone swimmingly for Manchester City and they are hoping it will get even better.

Once you get that sweet taste of long-awaited success, you want more, and coaches will tell you it is not reaching the top that is the hardest part, but staying there. Keeping hold of your best players is job No 1 in that regard, so persuading Khadija “Bunny” Shaw to perform a remarkable U-turn and stay for another four years was vital.

The Jamaica striker, who scored 21 times in 22 league games this season, had signalled firmly to the club she had decided to leave, because other teams were offering more lucrative contracts and talks with City had broken down. The late intervention of senior management from the men’s arm of the club to ensure Shaw’s contract requests were met led to her change of heart. She had made clear her preference was to stay and the club realised not only the value of keeping her, but the potential cost of her playing for a direct rival in Chelsea.

Shaw’s exit would have been a major momentum-killer. Her mic-drop-style reveal that she was staying, presented on stage during Monday’s trophy parade in Manchester in front of thousands of overjoyed fans, signalled that the club are serious about trying to build a winning machine and perhaps even challenge for a first European title.

The first stop is Wembley, where they face Brighton on Sunday when victory would land their first league and FA Cup Double and first two‑trophy season since 2019, when they lifted both domestic cups. It would also be their first FA Cup success in six years and their first in front of fans for seven years, because their extra-time victory over Everton in 2020 was played behind closed doors during the pandemic.

City will not have it all their own way against a Brighton side who beat them in the league in April and have been in tremendous form since mid-March, but the ambition of a confident City team, buoyed up by Shaw’s deal, is clear.

“Because we’ve won silverware, there’s more hunger there to win even more,” the midfielder Laura Blindkilde Brown says. “We were in the Champions League two years ago and we did well there and now it’s about trying to push on there and hopefully win that as well.”

View image in fullscreen ‘Because we’ve won silverware now, there’s more hunger there to win even more,’ says Laura Blindkilde Brown. Photograph: Naomi Baker/WSL/Getty Images

Perhaps the hardest thing for City in the fortnight since they lifted the WSL title has been finding a balance between celebrating and preparing. “We’re just trying to separate both, celebrate first and then really turn our focus on to Wembley,” Blindkilde Brown says.

The 22-year-old has been one of the team’s success stories this season and something of an unsung hero, playing in 20 of their 22 WSL games, starting 18 and demonstrating a maturity beyond her years as she controlled games from holding midfield. “I’ve really tried to put a mark on the season and make a name for myself,” she says. “We’ve really built connections in the midfield and every game I’m just improving more and more and there’s still so much for me to improve.”

The England international’s progress is another example of why the future looks so bright for the new champions and the core of their team looks capable of challenging on multiple fronts next term in their second season under the head coach, Andrée Jeglertz. There were four City players in the WSL’s team of the year, Shaw, Yui Hasegawa and Vivianne Miedema joined by the right-back Kerstin Casparij, who topped the league assist charts.

“All the puzzle pieces fitted together this year and also with Andrée coming in and with some incredible recruitment, players-wise, it all just fit; it’s felt so good,” Casparij said at last week’s WSL Football awards in London, where she was accepting Shaw’s WSL player of the year prize on her behalf.

Casparij does not want that to be the final trophy she gets her hands on this season. “To win a Double, after so many years, would be absolutely incredible,” she said. “That’s definitely a goal we have and we’ll give everything to realise that goal.”

Sports.title: Anthony Gordon signs for Barcelona and could be joined by Julian Alvarez – but where does this leave Marcus Rashford?
Sports.content:
Anthony Gordon signs for Barcelona and could be joined by Julian Alvarez – but where does this leave Marcus Rashford?

Barcelona have announced the signing of Anthony Gordon from Newcastle in a £70million deal.

The England winger has signed a five-year contract with the Spanish giants, which contains a 20 per cent sell-on clause, after they beat Bayern Munich to his signature.



4 Gordon could yet be joined by Rashford at Barcelona next season

Gordon had previously looked set for the Bundesliga champions, having previously agreed terms to join them.

However, Barca's sporting director Deco then held direct talks with Newcastle, despite indicating earlier this month the deal was too expensive to proceed with.

Better late than never

Speaking at his unveiling, where he impressively answered some questions in Spanish, Gordon confirmed he first heard of Barcelona's interest 'very late', but declared it was more than worth the wait.



"I found out very late from Barca," Gordon said.

"But as soon as I knew Barca was a serious option, there was never any question.

"I always wanted Barca. Barca is the biggest club on the planet.

"This is the stuff I dreamed of as a child. It really is a dream come true to be here."



How Gordon's Barca switch impacts Rashford

Gordon has now become the latest Englishman to head to Catalonia, after Marcus Rashford joined the club on loan last summer with an option to make the deal permanent for £26m.

talkSPORT understands the signing of Gordon does not necessarily rule out a future at Barcelona for Rashford, with manager Hansi Flick keen to keep to forward.



The LaLiga club have agreed personal terms with Rashford but are thought to favour another loan deal or a reduced fee, with United pushing for a permanent move.

4 Gordon is officially a Barcelona player

Barca's top priority after Gordon is thought to be Julian Alvarez, having seen a £86.8m bid rejected by Atletico Madrid.

In exchange for the ex-Manchester City star, Atleti want more than the £104m they spent on Antoine Griezmann in 2019.



If Barcelona's move for Alvarez falls through, this could also boost Rashford's chances of staying.

The United loanee has scored 14 goals and got 14 assists in 49 appearances this season and wishes to stay in Spain.

New chapter

For now though, Gordon is Barcelona's latest signing, who bids farewell to Newcastle after three year-and-a-half years on Tyneside.

He joined the Magpies from Everton in January 2023 in a deal worth up to £45m, in a huge signal of intent from the club.



4 Gordon was a standout player for Newcastle during his time at St James' Park Credit: AFP

4 The Englishman might be joined by Julian Alvarez, who could depart Atletico Madrid after just two seasons Credit: Getty

Since then, the 25-year-old made 152 appearances in all competitions, scoring 39 goals and delivering 28 assists.

Gordon twice helped the Magpies to secure Champions League qualification, in the 2022/23 campaign and again last term.



The crowning moment of his Newcastle career came in 2025, when he helped the club end a 70-year wait for a major trophy with Carabao Cup glory.

But the forward leaves St James' Park after a disappointing season, as the Toon Army finished a disappointing 12th in the Premier League.

Newcastle were also dumped out of the Champions League by Gordon's new club, Barcelona, suffering a humiliating 8-3 aggregate defeat in the round of 16.

Despite this, Gordon still managed an impressive 16 goals in all competitions, 10 of which came in Europe.



Having committed his future to Barcelona, he will now switch his focus to international duty, as he heads to the World Cup with England after being named in Thomas Tuchel's 26-man squad.

Sports.title: Atletico Madrid ruthlessly troll Barcelona after rejecting £86m bid for World Cup winner
Sports.content:
Atletico Madrid have posted THREE ruthless tweets regarding Barcelona's rejected offer for Julian Alvarez.

talkSPORT understands the Spanish giants have turned down an offer from the LaLiga champions worth £86million for Alvarez.



4 Alvarez is Barcelona's top transfer target to replace Robert Lewandowski

Atletico are looking for more than the £104m they received for selling Antoine Griezmann to Barca in 2019.

And in response to Barca's low offer, Diego Simeone's side have used social media to troll their rivals.

They have posted three tweets indirectly mocking Barcelona's Alvarez bid.



The first one is a reported transfer for Lamine Yamal from the Nou Camp to the Wanda Metropolitano.

It contains a picture of Yamal in an Atletico Madrid top along with the caption: "HERE WE GO! We have sent a fax to @FCBarcelona_es with our transfer offer: 4 tickets for tomorrow's Bad Bunny concert, an annual subscription to ABC, and a bag of sunflower seeds.



"We eagerly await the response to prepare the 'announce'."

And that was immediately followed up with another focusing on Pedri.

It was accompanied with these words: "HERE WE GO! For this second offer we've had a problem, we've run out of tickets for tomorrow's concert, so we improve the previous proposal with 6 for the one on Sunday."

And the third one featured Raphinha, which read: "HERE WE GO! And to complete the 3x1, we've gotten all carried away and we're going to throw the little house out the window: the player arrives on loan for a season and in exchange we loan out Tom Ford and Smith with no option to buy. An offer impossible to refuse."



Bad blood

Clearly, Atletico Madrid haven't taken too kindly to the Alvarez offer on the table.

The Catalan giants have already spoken to the Argentine's agents, and he is keen on the deal.

Reports suggest that personal terms won't be a problem for Barcelona to agree.

They are looking to strike a quick deal before other clubs can react, with Arsenal one of several sides who are big admirers of Alvarez.



The former Manchester City man actually helped dump Barcelona out of the Champions League earlier this season with a stunning free-kick at the Nou Camp.

But he is the club's top target to replace Robert Lewandowski, who is leaving on a free after a successful stint with Barcelona.

4 Alvarez's goal in the Champions League against Barcelona was a moment of pure class Credit: AFP

4 Simeone's side have torn into Barcelona Credit: AFP



Are they back?

The early signs this summer suggest that after years of being restrained in the transfer market due to financial issues, Barcelona are back.

They are poised to sign Anthony Gordon from Newcastle United in a deal that moved rapidly.

Bayern Munich were leading the chase for the England international but were struggled to agree a fee with the Toon.

Hansi Flick's side swooped in and offered £70m plus add-ons that could take the deal towards £80m along with a healthy sell-on clause.



The winger has completed a medical and agreed terms on a five-year deal and will be unveiled soon.

4 Gordon's only experience of the Nou Camp was a 7-2 defeat in the Champions League Credit: Getty

And they aren't done there.

The Times are reporting that Bernardo Silva wants to join Barca after leaving Manchester City.

The Portuguese international has long been linked with a move to the Nou Camp, and it could finally happen this summer.



His contract at the Etihad is up, and he's leaving the club a legend.

There is also a player from the other side of Manchester that Barcelona could still sign.

Marcus Rashford spent the season on loan with Flick's side and impressed with 14 goals and 14 assists across all competitions.

Barcelona have an option to buy him for £26m from Manchester United.

But talkSPORT understands they want another loan deal instead, so that one could drag on.

But it is clear they mean business.

Sports.title: Lincoln lose manager weeks after promotion as new Championship rivals swoop in
Sports.content:
Lincoln lose manager weeks after promotion as new Championship rivals swoop in

Bristol City have confirmed the appointment of Michael Skubala as their new manager on a three-year deal.

Skubala has swapped Lincoln City for Ashton Gate after guiding the Imps into the Championship.

3 Bristol have hired Skubala from newly-promoted Championship side Lincoln Credit: Getty

He had been in charge of Lincoln since November 2023.

It marked his first permanent managerial role in first-team football after a year as Leeds United's under-21 manager.

He has also previously worked with England's under-18 side as well as spells managing at Nottingham Forest and Coventry City's academies.

Skubala will be replaced at Lincoln by Chris Cohen and Tom Shaw, who make the step up from their previous roles as assistant head coaches.

The 2025/26 season saw Lincoln secure promotion from League One as champions under the 43-year-old.

Their 103-point haul clinched a return to the second-tier for the first time in 65 years.

Skubala's side won 31 of their 46 league matches, losing just five times in League One all season.

After securing promotion in April, they ended the campaign 12 points clear of second place Cardiff City.

In an emotional goodbye statement to Lincon's fans, Skubala said: "I want to say a huge thank you to everyone connected with Lincoln City for the support I’ve received during my time here.

“I’ve loved being part of this football club. There is a special connection between the team and the fans, and I’ve felt that from day one.

3 Skubala guided Lincoln to the League One title after 65 years away from the second-tier Credit: Getty

“I’m proud of what we achieved together and being able to lead this club to the Championship for the first time in 65 years was a true honour.

“I am so grateful for the relationships and memories that have been created along the way. Lincoln City and the club’s fans will always be in my heart and mean so much to me, and I wish the club nothing but success in the future. Up the Imps.”

Bristol City's manager hunt

Bristol City had been on the looking for a new permanent manager following Gerhard Struber's sacking in March.

The Austrian was replaced by Roy Hodgson on an interim basis for the final seven matches of the season.

Hodgson subsequently guided the club to a 12th place finish, although they ended the campaign 11 points adrift of the play-offs.

It means the Robins will now embark on their 12th successive season in the Championship next term.

3 Skubala had been in charge of Lincoln since November 2013 Credit: Getty

Following Hodgson's departure at the end of the campaign, a number of candidates emerged for the Bristol City job.

Talks were previously held with Portsmouth boss John Mousinho after he secured Championship survival with Pompey.

Meanwhile, the club also approached Bournemouth's Tommy Elphick earlier this month.

Though Cherries' assistant manager is set to remain at the Vitality Stadium, though, as part of new boss Marco Rose's backroom team.

Sports.title: Jurgen Klopp eyed for return to management as ex-Liverpool boss made ‘dream’ target
Sports.content:
Jurgen Klopp eyed for return to management as ex-Liverpool boss made ‘dream’ target

Jurgen Klopp is the 'dream' target for Saudi Arabian side Al-Ittihad as their new manager, talkSPORT understands.

The German has been out of managerial work since departing Liverpool in the summer of 2024.

4 Klopp's reputation stands him out as one of the best managers in the world Credit: AFP

During his tenure at Anfield, Liverpool were crowned Premier League champions for the first time and narrowly missed out on others to Manchester City.

They won the Champions League as well as every other trophy available, including the Club World Cup and UEFA Super Cup.

The former Broussia Dortmund boss is currently the Global Head of Soccer for Red Bull.

But Al-Ittihad would love to convince him to get back into management.

talkSPORT's Ben Jacobs reports that the club have genuine interest in trying to appoint Klopp.

They are on the lookout for a new manager after Francisco Conceição left.

However, deal-makers at the club feel it would be near impossible to recruit Klopp.

Adding to the difficulty of the deal is Al-Ittihad's financial position, with backing from the Saudi Ministry of Finance the only solution to help fund a deal for Klopp.

Club insiders have told talkSPORT that Klopp remains a dream target, but downplayed any suggestion of advanced talks.

The German's agent, Marc Kosicke, has also released a short statement, courtesy of Ismael Mahmoud and winwin.

4 Klopp will always be a Liverpool legend and also created some exciting teams that blew the opposition away Credit: Getty

He said: “There is NO possibility for Klopp to manage Al-Ittihad this year”.

Will Klopp return to management?

Following Klopp's departure from Liverpool, he has been linked with a number of vacant posts across Europe's elite teams.

Earlier this year, following Xabi Alonso being sacked by Real Madrid, Klopp was rumoured to be in contention to replace the Spaniard at the Bernabeu.

Ultimately a deal never eventuated and Jose Mourinho is now poised to return for a second spell after a brief spell in Portugal with Benfica.

But when asked about managing Real, Klopp made it clear that he isn't done with management just yet.

He said: "If Real Madrid had phoned, we would have heard about it by now.

4 Klopp managed 489 games as Liverpool manager and put himself into the history books Credit: Getty

"But that's all nonsense. They haven't called even once, not once. My agent is there, you can ask him. They haven't called him either.

"Right now I'm not thinking about that, luckily there's no reason to.

"For my age I'm quite advanced in life, but as a coach I'm not completely finished. I haven't reached retirement age.

"Who knows what will happen in the coming years? But there's nothing planned."

One certainty

However, any Premier League fans hoping that Klopp will one day rock up need to prepare for disappointment.

That's because after nine years with Liverpool and numerous trophies, he vowed never to manage team in England.

4 Alongside managing Liverpool, Klopp has coached Mainz and Borussia Dortmund Credit: Getty

"What I know definitely is that I will never, ever manage a different club in England than Liverpool, 100 per cent. That's not possible," Klopp said.

But a return to Anfield certainly isn't off the cards.

Speaking in October 2025, Klopp said: "I said I will never coach a different team in England so that means, if [I did return], then it's Liverpool.

"So, yeah, theoretically it is possible.

"I don't even know exactly. I love what I do now. I don't miss coaching. I don't. I do coach but it's just different, it's not players.

"I don't miss it. I don't miss standing in the rain for two-and-a-half or three hours. I also don't miss going to press conferences three times a week.

"Having 10 or 12 interviews a week, I don't miss that. I don't. I don't miss being in the dressing room. I coached around 1,080 games so I was in the dressing room very, very often.

"I don't want to die in the dressing room. It's these kind of things. I'm 58. From your perspective that might be old, but from other perspectives, it's not that old.

"That means I could make a decision in a few years. I don't know. Do I have to make a decision today? I will not coach again, but thank God I do not have to do that, I can just see what the future brings."

Sports.title: Laura Woods makes special announcement hours after returning on talkSPORT
Sports.content:
Laura Woods has announced that she is expecting her second child with fiancé Adam Collard.

The former talkSPORT Breakfast host has been in a relationship with the ex-Love Island contestant since 2023, with the couple welcoming their first-born, Leo, in January 2025.

5 Woods and Collard are expecting their second child Credit: instagram / @laurawoodsy

5 The pair shared a picture of their ultrasound scan in a heartwarming Instagram post Credit: Instagram @adamcollard

And the pair have now taken to Instagram to share the exciting news of their growing family.

'Baby number 2'

In a joint-post, the couple shared a scan of their unborn baby, with Collard captioning it: "Hey, baby number 2.”

This was included in a reel of images, which also showed their first-born, Leo, looking at a big projection of the scan.

Rounding off the post was clip of a popular meme showing a woman saying: "You're joking. Not another one."

Woods and Collard were quickly inundated with congratulations from friends and fans, including many of the talkSPORT family.

Gabby Agbonlahor, who often co-hosted the Breakfast Show alongside Woods, wrote: "Congrats," followed by a heart emoji.

talkSPORT presenter Olivia Buzaglo also passed on her well wishes, commenting: "Congratulations," alongside a stream of hearts.

Woods and Collard welcomed a son, Leo, in at the start of last year, 15 months after first going public with their relationship.

In July 2024, the TNT Sports presenter announced she was pregnant with their first child, and the pair got engaged in September of the same year.

Busy day

The happy news comes just hours after Woods made a stunning one-off return to talkSPORT Breakfast.

5 Woods and Collard shared a picture of their first-born Leo looking at a projection of their scan Credit: Instagram @adamcollard

5 The exciting news came just hours after Woods returned to host talkSPORT Breakfast Credit: talkSPORT

With her beloved Gunners playing in the Champions League final against Paris Saint-Germain on Saturday, she reunited with co-host Ally McCoist live from Budapest to preview a huge night for her club, thanks to talkSPORT's partnership with TNT Sports.

The popular figure previously presented the Breakfast Show between 2020 and 2023.

Since leaving, Woods has worked for TNT Sports on their Champions League evenings, and will be fronting their coverage of Saturday's final.

But before that, she was back in familiar surroundings as she joined up with old pal McCoist to talk all things Gunners.

And Woods gave us a glimpse into family life on the show, as she revealed she is raising son Leo to follow in her lead in becoming an Arsenal fan, although she faces a battle with Geordie fiancé Collard, who is a big Newcastle supporter.

The presenter had a firm response when quizzed by McCoist if she would ever allow her first-born to play for bitter rivals Tottenham if he grew up to be a talented footballer.

5 Woods will be heading up TNT Sports' Champions League final coverage Credit: Getty

Woods' reply was immediate, as she insisted: “No", before hilariously explaining herself.

She continued: “I want my son to do the best in life.

“And I think whatever happens, if he's a professional footballer - congratulations, that's incredible.

“Who do you want to sign for? Spurs? Absolutely not.

“You know what, you've got more to learn on this planet before making those decisions.

“And if he made a decision that would take him to the wrong side of north London, he would be in trouble.”

Sports.title: Piers Morgan makes wild promise if Arsenal win Champions League final: ‘I apologise for nothing’
Sports.content:
Piers Morgan plans to emulate John Terry's infamous Champions League final antics if Arsenal beat Paris Saint-Germain.

The Gunners face the French giants at the Puskas Arena in the final on Saturday night.



3 Morgan has revealed how he plans to celebrate if Arsenal win the Champions League Credit: Alamy

It marks the club's first appearance in the showpiece contest since 2006 as they aim to become European champions for the first time.

Following their Premier League triumph, Mikel Arteta's side now face the holders after PSG beat Inter Milan in last year's final.

Morgan is already planning his celebrations in the event his beloved Arsenal beat the Ligue 1 champions this weekend.



The broadcaster celebrated the club's league title win with several members of the squad on Sunday.

He had been invited onto the pitch at Selhurst Park for the trophy lift after attending their final day victory over Crystal Palace.



Despite being criticised by some for joining the squad's post-match party, Morgan has vowed to do the same if they beat PSG.

The 61-year-old has even promised to go a step further and sport a full Arsenal kit in similar fashion to Terry in 2012.



Terry infamously ran onto the pitch in his Chelsea strip after they beat Bayern Munich to win the Champions League 14 years ago.

His antics came despite the then Blues captain missing the match through suspension.

However, it did not stop Terry from lifting the trophy in his full Chelsea kit.

3 Terry infamously celebrate Chelsea's 2012 triumph in full kit despite not playing the final Credit: News Group Newspapers Ltd



Morgan's full kit celebration

Morgan joined Ally McCoist and TNT Sports' Laura Woods on Friday's talkSPORT Breakfast show to look ahead to the final.

Revealing his plans, he explained: "I’ve had a bit of stick for having the audacity to accept an invitation having paid full price for four tickets two months ago to Selhurst Park for what turned out to be the trophy fun.

"Then I got invited to the chairman’s lounge, had a great time, met all the Arsenal guys and then got invited to go down to pitchside for the trophy lift.

"If there’s an Arsenal fan on God’s earth who would have said no in that moment I’d like their name and details please. So as Conor McGregor would say, I apologise for absolutely nothing.



"If we win the Champions League tomorrow night, I am bringing a full Arsenal kit to Budapest and if we win the Champions League, I’m pulling a full John Terry everybody."

Arsenal's Champions League hopes

Arsenal will be appearing in the Champions League final for only the second time in their history.

3 Morgan was on the pitch for Arsenal's Premier League trophy lift last weekend Credit: Instagram / @piersmorgan

Their previous appearance ended in a 2-1 defeat to Barcelona back in 2006.



On this occasion, they take on PSG in Budapest, with kick-off at 5pm on Saturday live on talkSPORT.

Adrian Durham will host live coverage and commentary of the match from 3.30pm.

As well as winning their first Premier League title for 22 years this season, Arsenal are also unbeaten in the Champions League this term.

They have picked up 11 wins and three draws from their 14 matches so far in the competition.



However, they lost both legs of last season's semi-final to PSG the last time the two sides met.

Sports.title: Arsenal vs Paris Saint-Germain predictions: Gunners overwhelmingly backed for first Champions League crown
Sports.content:
Arsenal have the tools required to beat Paris Saint-Germain and scoop their first Champions League title.

That's the view of many pundits across the talkSPORT network as the Gunners battle the holders in the final at the Puskas Arena in Budapest on Saturday.

12 Arsenal are looking to win a historic first Premier League and Champions League double Credit: Getty

Mikel Arteta's men and Luis Enrique's rampant side will face off for the second season running at 5pm - live on talkSPORT.

Arteta won his first meeting against his compatriot as Arsenal won 2-0 in their league phase encounter last term, before losing both semi-final legs.

Both teams go into this weekend's contest having won their domestic league, with the north London outfit finally ending their 22-year wait for top-flight glory.

And it's the feelgood factor around the Emirates which has so many fans hopeful that they can lift 'Old Big Ears' for the first time in club history.

Gunner do it?

Arsenal are the only side in this season's tournament who remain unbeaten.

Unsurprisingly, they boast the best defensive record having conceded just six goals, while keeping nine clean sheets from their 14 outings.

But they are up against a PSG team that are the top scorers with 44 goals.

Winger Khvicha Kvaratskhelia has been directly involved in 16 of those strikes, having chipped in with 10 goals and six assists.

PSG are the bookmakers' favourites to win a second consecutive Champions League, and for good reason, having dismantled Monaco, Chelsea, Liverpool and Bayern Munich in the knockout rounds.

The stage is set for what promises to be one of the most fascinating finals in recent memory, with many telling talkSPORT that Arsenal can end their European hoodoo on their 240th match in the competition.

12 PSG are looking to become just the ninth team to win back-to-back Champions League titles Credit: AFP

Piers Morgan - Arsenal

Speaking on the talkSPORT Breakfast show, Arsenal fan and broadcaster Piers Morgan said: "Yeah, I think we're going to beat them.

"And the reason, I think we have the best goalkeeper in the world, I think we have the best back four in the world.

"And crucially, even like I say, when we lose our first choice right-back, [Jurrien] Timber, who's been brilliant, I don't think he's probably going to make it, but maybe he will.

"Then we lose Ben White, which other team in the world could bring in a player as your third choice right-back in [Cristhian] Moquera, who then plays as well as he's been playing when he's had to come in?

"So this is the genius of Arteta in the way they've got this squad together and the genius of [Andrea] Berta and the others who've got these players in.

"So I think it's the squad depth which is going to work for us in Budapest, plus all the pressures off, when you win something like the Premier League, then all the pressure goes - 22 years of hurt and pain have just dissipated in one fell swoop.

"They look so happy, so relieved, the pressure's off, nobody expects us to go and beat PSG, apart from us, Arsenal fans, and apart from Mikel Arteta and Declan Rice and this team of warriors who I think are going to go over to Hungary and they're going to beat them."

12 Arsenal are riding high after being crowned champions of England Credit: Getty

Alan Pardew - 50/50

The talkSPORT co-host remarked: "I watched them [Arsenal], I was thinking, 'Right, OK, just put your head on, you're going to play them next week. What would you do? How would you hurt them?'

"There's not really much you can do to hurt them, and PSG are going to find that - particularly if Timber's fit in the Champions League.

"People are thinking that PSG have got a game here that more than favourites to win it.

"I don't see it like that because I think PSG probably haven't come up against a defensive side as good as Arsenal, and I'm talking about from their offensive players, let alone the defenders.

"So they're going to find it difficult, they've got obviously the best defensive line probably in world football at the moment.

"But that is going to be a really great game of great defenders against great, probably the best defensive team, so I'm looking forward to that."

12 William Saliba and Gabriel Magalhaes are regarded as one of Europe's best centre-back partnerships Credit: Getty

Ally McCoist - PSG

The talkSPORT Breakfast co-host said: "They [Arsenal] are going to have to defend like never before again.

"That said I fancy PSG. I've got to be brutally honest, I just do.

"I just think their games against Bayern Munich did of course show a vulnerability in defence, right?

"But I'm not sure Arsenal is as good going forward as Bayern Munich are, that would be a concern, but I take what they are.

"They're better at set plays than probably every other team in Europe, so they have a chance to score.

"But I just think there's so many dangerous areas in the PSG side, there's so many potential match winners."

12 Kvaratskhelia is in lethal form - Arsenal must keep him quiet to stand any chance of lifting the trophy Credit: Getty

Simon Jordan - Arsenal

He stated on the White and Jordan show: "I think Arsenal will fancy this game, I think Arsenal can defend, we've seen that PSG can concede.

"We've seen that they can concede at significant times in the game, in the game that Chelsea lost 5-2, I don't quite know how Chelsea managed to conspire to lose that game 5-2 because they were dominating certain parts of that game, we've seen Munich do it.

"Arsenal can defend, they can defend probably better than any of the opposition that PSG have played against in this campaign.

"If I was looking at it from the point of view of putting odds on it, I'd say 60-40 PSG.

"But I fancy Arsenal to win this game, I think Arsenal can go into this game full of beans, full of confidence."

12 Arsenal are in their first European Cup final since losing to Barcelona in 2006

Lauren - 50/50

The two-time Premier League champion stated on the talkSPORT Breakfast show: "I believe that if Arsenal stop PSG running, because you know, they can kill you on quick transition.

"So what we have to do is to control, stop them with the possession of the ball, if we have that possession of the ball as long as possible during the 90 minutes, then we will have big chances in order to win the game.

"Because we know that if we go like an open game, up and down, quick transition, PSG, they will kill you.

"We saw that against Bayern Munich in the semi-final, we have to stop them running.

"And to be able to stop them running, we have to control the possession of the ball the longest time as possible."

12 Arsenal icon Lauren was part of the last squad that reached the Champions League final Credit: Getty

Martin Keown - 50/50

talkSPORT and TNT Sports pundit and Arsenal Invincible Keown meanwhile said: "Declan Rice is going to have to have the game of his life for Arsenal to win.

"I often refer to him as having two engines, and his second one kicks into gear in the Champions League, he’s won quite a few man-of-the-match awards in Europe this season, he’s been really dominant."

He continued: "Arsenal probably have the two best central defenders in Europe.

"They are formidable, and they will need to be in that form to keep Ousmane Dembele, Desire Doue, and Kvaratskhelia quiet."

Keown finished by saying: "Arsenal will get opportunities, and is this goalkeeper [Matvey Safonov] going to be good enough stop them?"

12 Keown believes Arsenal's defence and midfield will be crucial in their clash against PSG Credit: Getty

Emmanuel Petit - 50/50

The ex-Arsenal midfielder said on the White and Jordan show: "Look Paris Saint-Germain in the eyes, come on the pitch, play your own football, you have to forget about how they play.

"You have to put something personal on the pitch, you come on the pitch and you want to win that final, it doesn't matter who's playing, who you're going to against.

"And I think this is for me the solution, if I am an Arsenal player, I will come into that final thinking, 'OK, all right, listen, guys, for 16 months now, this team has been the worst team to beat on the planet.

"'They have amazing players, they are so goo, collectively, but it doesn't matter, we have qualities, we are strong, we just won the Premier League, the toughest league in the world.

"We're in the Champions League [final], we've been one of the most improving teams for the last three, four years now, so we have the quality to hurt them as well.'"

12 Arsenal are out for revenge after PSG beat them in the Champions League semi-final last season Credit: Getty

Julien Laurens - 50/50

The PSG fan and broadcaster told talkSPORT: "It's going to be a great final, I think it's much tighter than a lot of people seem to think.

"Because there's no, 'PSG as strong favourites,' or anything like that, but I think Arsenal have the game to disturb the way PSG play.

"If there's a team that can control the tempo, it's Arsenal, they're the best at that, they're the best team out of possession when they don't have the ball.

"They're so difficult to play against, they're so physical, they're so well organised that I think this is everything that you need to cause problems to PSG."

Before adding: "But I also think PSG, having been in the final last season, that kind of experience is so important when you go into a final like this, even from an Arsenal team that has less pressure because they've won the league title now, which was the objective at the start of the season.

"I think it's a big advantage for PSG to have been there before and also to be able to go back-to-back."

12 PSG have already beaten Arsenal's Premier League rivals Liverpool, Chelsea and Tottenham this term Credit: AFP

Dean Saunders - Arsenal

The ex-Liverpool striker told talkSPORT: "I just think Arsenal can beat them, I might be wrong, the bookies normally get it right.

"But I just think if there's a team that can stop PSG [it's Arsenal]... and my thinking behind it is, the back four.

"Arsenal's back four, 6'4, 6'5, 6'4, 6'4, dangerous from set plays and can head corners out of their own box."

Saunders continued: "They haven't got a player with a bad attitude."

He concluded by saying: "But going the other way, I don't think PSG's defence can stop Arsenal."

12 Arsenal's physicality could be a deciding factor against Les Parisiens Credit: Getty

Tom Hiddleston - Arsenal

Speaking on talkSPORT Drive ahead of Soccer Aid on Sunday, the Hollywood actor and Arsenal fan said: "For Arsenal, they've had their opening night, they've won the Premier League.

"And so this is the next show, and they'll be playing with wind beneath their wings, no pressure, there will just be that sense of freedom.

"I think if they hadn't won the Premier League, there would be this tension.

"And now they've got something and they know they're champions, so the best team in England, which is the best league in the world, it's a really hard league to win.

"And I think, in the words of Alan Shearer, if there's a team to beat PSG, it's Arsenal."

12 British actor Hiddleston believes the pressure is off Arsenal going into the final Credit: talkSPORT

Liam Brady - Arsenal

Arsenal legend Brady told talkSPORT: "We've never won it, we were a little bit unlucky against Barcelona in Paris [in 2006].

"That's got to be nearly 20 years ago as well, so it's going to be a big night.

"But we're going into the game stress-free now, after winning the title, absolutely stress-free.

"And I I could see us beating Paris Saint-Germain, maybe by a goal to nil.

"We're good defensively, they're brilliant going forward, it's going to be a wonderful night.
